description: BattLeDIM 2020, the Battle of the Leakage Detection and Isolation Methods, is a benchmark competition for detecting and locating leaks in water distribution networks from SCADA flow and pressure measurements. It is built on L-Town, a hypothetical small town whose EPANET model and SCADA data were generated from a real distribution network in a city in Cyprus and which suffers many pipe breaks and water losses. Participants received a historical SCADA dataset for 2018 and an evaluation dataset for 2019 and had to report the time and location of the leaks that occurred in 2019. The site offers the dataset as a download, with rules, results and workshop material; a Code Ocean capsule (v1.1, November 2024) holds the L-TOWN input file, the competition data, the true leakages and the scoring algorithm. It was organised by the KIOS centre at the University of Cyprus with TU Delft, Technion and Tsinghua, and is described by Vrachimis et al. (2022) with a special collection of papers. Caveats: the network and data are simulated, the competition is closed and no licence name was shown on the pages read. Simulation uses: testing leak detection for water digital twins, hydraulic network models and sensor placement. Related records: BATADAL (data-batadal-attack-detection-datasets), LeakDB (data-leakdb) and EPANET (model-epanet).
